key_insight: Fault-tolerant spin-qubit quantum computers may become energy-competitive before they become time-competitive, with cryogenic cooling, control, and decoding dominating the power budget.
engineering_relevance: The paper provides a practical energy roadmap for scaling semiconductor spin-qubit systems, showing where architecture and control design can cut energy by orders of magnitude.
method: Built an energy budget for a Loss-DiVincenzo spin-qubit quantum computer
Compared Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) energy use against classical FFT under polynomial sampling assumptions
Extended the analysis to surface-code QEC, including gate synthesis, decoding, and cryogenic overheads
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that for about one million physical qubits the estimated power draw is roughly 100 kW, and optimizing control demultiplexing can reduce total energy by around two orders of magnitude.
watch_item: The conclusions depend on modeling assumptions for cryogenic, instrumentation, and decoding overheads, so real hardware implementations may differ significantly.
paper_title: Energetics of Fault-Tolerant Spin-Qubit Quantum Computation
